## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates expertise in cross-process IPC, memory ordering semantics, and memory reclamation in NUMA environments under realistic contention scenarios.

## Key Concepts
- Cross-process lock-free data structures
- Memory ordering: acquire/release fences and sequence counters
- False sharing prevention through cache-line padding
- Epoch-based reclamation across process boundaries
- NUMA-aware performance optimization
- Microbenchmark design for IPC throughput and latency analysis

## Code Example
```c
typedef struct {
    uint64_t seq;
    uint8_t payload[128];
```

## Implementation Details
The queue uses a circular buffer with sequence numbers to track slot ownership. Each slot has a 64-bit sequence number that ensures proper synchronization between producers and consumers without locks. The padded head/tail indices prevent false sharing on cache lines.

## Performance Considerations
NUMA-aware placement of shared memory regions minimizes cross-node memory access. The spin-wait approach is suitable for high-throughput scenarios where the queue is rarely empty or full.

## Benchmarking Strategy

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests cross-NUMA IPC design with ABA avoidance, memory ordering, and cache-line discipline for senior systems positions.

## Key Concepts
- Cross-NUMA memory allocation and cache coherence
- Per-slot sequencing to prevent ABA problems
- Acquire/release semantics for proper memory ordering
- Cache-line padding to avoid false sharing
- Backpressure handling and wrap-around logic
- NUMA-aware process binding and memory pinning

## Technical Accuracy
- 40 Gbps requires ~5GB/s throughput, achievable with this design
- 64-bit sequence numbers prevent ABA even with wrap-around
- Cache-line alignment (64 bytes) prevents false sharing
- Memory fences ensure proper ordering across NUMA domains
- Fixed 128-byte slots with 112-byte payload meet requirements
- Capacity 1<<18 (262144 slots) provides 32MB buffer space

- How would you extend to N producers and M consumers with fairness guarantees?
- What failure modes matter under NUMA remapping or node failure?
- How would you handle variable-sized payloads efficiently?
- What optimizations for specific CPU architectures (Intel vs AMD)?
